name: Fishing
migratedFrom: guides218.json professions[10] (2026-11-04), rewritten into the course format on 2026-11-12

overview.lead: Fishing supplies the seafood for several reworked raid foods and has camp objects of its own.

points.text: The Fish Bowl gives 8% to all stats and does not stack with Blessing of Kings.

101.summary: Fishing's camp objects and how to level it.

steps.text: Place a Fish Bowl at Fishing 20, a Fishing Rack at 140 and a Fishing Hut at 300.
Get the Fishing Rack blueprint from Gelihast in Blackfathom Deeps.
Add your object to a camp, then sit or craft nearby for about a minute. The benefits last an hour.

mistakes.mistake: Expecting a trainer to sell the Fishing Rack.
mistakes.fix: Trainers and NPCs hand out the skill-20 camp objects. The Fishing Rack comes from a blueprint that drops from Gelihast in Blackfathom Deeps.

steps.text: Fishing tops out at 300, like the other professions.
Artisan Fishing comes from Nat Pagle at level 35.
Take the Luremaster Legacy perk for a chance of an extra fish.

mistakes.mistake: Expecting to learn Artisan Fishing before level 35.
mistakes.fix: Artisan Fishing comes from Nat Pagle at level 35.

201.summary: What Fishing adds to a group and to the market.

chapters.title: The Fish Bowl and raid seafood

steps.text: Place the Fish Bowl in groups without a Paladin. It gives 8% to all stats, a little under the 10% from Blessing of Kings, and does not stack with it.
Fish for your cook: Grilled Squid, Hot Smoked Bass, Baked Salmon and Lobster Stew are seafood dishes.

mistakes.mistake: Placing the Fish Bowl for a group that already has Blessing of Kings.
mistakes.fix: The Fish Bowl's 8% does not stack with the 10% from Blessing of Kings, so it adds nothing there.

steps.text: Cooks need fish for several reworked raid foods, so a steady catch should find buyers. Trading is subject to Blizzard policy.

mistakes.fix: Several reworked raid foods, such as Grilled Squid and Lobster Stew, are seafood dishes, so raid cooks buy fish too.
